transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-07
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Meeting ID: ff-20260507-9f7b
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortega (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (StratusDocs Head of Search), Ben Kwok (Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (Data Scientist)

Summary:
- Initial scoping for a PoC to replace a legacy Confluence search with embeddings + rerank. Exploring hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment given PII and on-prem content.
- Key asks: throughput targets for 100 QPS at peak with sub-120ms tail for rerank path, storage of embeddings in a vector DB (weave/pc?), embedding dims tradeoffs, and security controls (SSO, KMS, audit logs).
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send PoC plan and benchmark steps; StratusDocs to share sample export and eval queries.

Topics: PoC goals, vector DB options, embedding dimensionality, hybrid search, inference routing, VPC/SAML, cost projections

Action items (in call):
- Maya to share PoC doc and pricing sheet
- Rafael to propose benchmark scripts and SSH-friendly test harness
- Ben to provide sample data set and credentials for staging VPC
- Sofia to produce 50-query relevance set

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we should probably do a quick intros then jump into what you're trying to accomplish with Confluence search.
[00:18] Asha Patel (StratusDocs): Hi, thanks. I'm Asha. brief context: our docs are in Confluence across 14 spaces, internal + customer facing. Search is pretty bad, exact-match heavy. We want embeddings + rerank to surface right docs and surface policy approved content.
[00:36] Ben Kwok (StratusDocs): Ben here, we run the platform infra, currently using ES clusters but embeddings storage has been kind of ad-hoc, we've looked at Pinecone and Milvus.
[00:45] Rafael Ortega (Redwood): Great. quick Q: are you more inclined to hosted Redwood or would you need a private deployment?
[00:54] Asha: Security is a huge factor; we have contracts with customers that require data to remain in our VPC and some docs contain PII. So Private or Dedicated with VPC peering. Also need KMS integration.
[01:12] Maya: Ok good to know. We support Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deploys (VPC/on-prem). For KMS we can federate to your KMS or use our HSM -- we'll share the integration guide.
[01:30] Sofia Martinez (StratusDocs): On the model / embedding side, we're evaluating dims - right now using 384 dims from an off-the-shelf model. We wonder about tradeoffs moving to 768 or 1024 for better recall vs storage and query latency.
[01:50] Rafael: Typical tradeoff — higher dims increase index size and per-query compute. For reranking path: you might run a two-step flow: sparse retrieval (BM25) or hybrid retrieval against vector DB at 384, then rerank with a model using a higher-dim embedding or cross-encoder. Redwood supports hybrid routing and model fallback so you can set policy by latency SLOs.
[02:15] Ben: We need to hit ~100 QPS peak for search queries across internal users; 95th percentile latency target is <120ms for the fetch+rerank pipeline. Is that realistic?
[02:30] Rafael: It's doable but depends on batching, KV cache warm up, and whether rerank is on CPU or GPU. On Dedicated / Private with GPUs we can keep tails low. Hosted can do it but may require reserved capacity. We'll propose a config.
[02:55] Asha: Also curious about vector DB integration: we have a preference for self-hosted Milvus but would consider a managed Pinecone if it meets security. Can Redwood point to recommended vector DBs and supported connectivity?
[03:10] Maya: Yes, our customers use Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate and also Postgres + FAISS setups. For Private we can co-locate Redwood inference nodes with your vector DB in the same VPC. We'll include connector patterns in the doc.
[03:30] Sofia: can you explain hybrid search in more detail; we saw a doc but want to understand how ranker + retriever interplay works in practice.
[03:45] Rafael: Sure. common pattern: generate embedding for query -> search vector DB to retrieve top-k -> optionally expand/promote with BM25 hybrid scoring -> send top-n candidates to rerank model. Redwood supports continuous batching for rerank and automatic fallback to cheaper model variant if capacity is constrained. There are knobs for prefix caching for often-seen queries which helps tail latency.
[04:15] Ben: How do you handle embedding versioning and reconciliation when we re-embed on a new model? Our corp wiki has 6M docs. Re-embedding everything is expensive.
[04:27] Maya: We support model version pinning and staged rollouts. For big re-embeds we recommend a rolling sharding approach and can do delta-embedding updates. We'll send a template strategy in the PoC doc.
[04:45] Asha: On the security checklist, we need SOC2 type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, field-level encryption. Can Redwood provide compliance artifacts?
[04:58] Maya: Yes. we'll share SOC2 report, and our SAML SSO and RBAC docs. For audit logs and retention that's configurable on Dedicated/Private. Also KMS key control is available for Private.
[05:20] Sofia: In terms of benchmarks, what does Redwood measure? We want reproducible bench for throughput and relevance.
[05:30] Rafael: We'll measure QPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies for embedding and rerank paths, tokens per second for model inference, and end-to-end relevance with your eval set (MRR / NDCG). We'll provide harness scripts.
[05:50] Ben: Any gotchas with Confluence export? Our pages have attachments, macros, and some nested comments — we only want the body content for embeddings.
[06:04] Sofia: also we need anonymization.
[06:07] Maya: Good call. Ben, can you provide an anonymized export? even 2000 pages will be fine for the PoC.
[06:17] Ben: yes we can do a sanitized dump. I'll scope which spaces.
[06:25] Asha: timeline-wise we want a PoC within 4 weeks and evaluate results with product stakeholders. Customer procurement may take another 2-3 weeks after the PoC.
[06:38] Rafael: Sounds reasonable. For a 4 week PoC we'll propose a minimal infra: Redwood Dedicated trial nodes or Private staging, vector DB (Milvus in your VPC), and a small eval harness.
[06:52] Maya: Pricing note: we can do a time-limited discounted Dedicated commit for PoC to make benching predictable — we'll include numbers.
[07:02] Ben: Regarding storage, do you have suggestions for dimension reduction or quantization to reduce index size?
[07:11] Rafael: We support quantized execution for inference (int8/4) and for embeddings you can use PQ on the vector DB side. There's also combined strategies — use 768 dims and PQ to reduce memory. We'll run trials.
[07:28] Speaker 2 (transcript error): umm sorry is this about para text or parallel ops?
[07:34] Rafael: I think that was just a slip, the main point is the tradeoff.
[07:40] Sofia: For relevance eval, we can produce 50 queries with expected correct doc IDs. We'll run NDCG and precision@k.
[07:50] Maya: Perfect. We'll align metrics and baseline (your current ES-based recall).
[08:02] Asha: One more question — do you offer automatic fallback to smaller models during spikes to keep cost down?
[08:12] Rafael: Yes — routing policies can fall back to a cheaper model, or to cached responses. For mission-critical flows, we can also configure canary and A/B rollouts.
[08:25] Ben: Network topology: if we go Private, we'll need a package that runs in our VPC and talk to our Milvus cluster. Does Redwood provide an appliance or Helm charts?
[08:36] Maya: For Private we provide an OSS-like package and Helm charts for k8s, plus an installer for air-gapped on-prem. We'll send the deployment guide.
[08:50] Sofia: Any similar customers in regulated spaces?
[08:55] Maya: Yes, we have a healthcare customer and a financial services pilot; they use Private with KMS and strict RBAC. We'll anonymize case studies.
[09:07] Asha: About costs — do you charge embeddings storage separately or is that part of vector DB cost?
[09:15] Maya: Embedding generation is billed per token/embedding on the Redwood inference side; storage is separate — usually on your vector DB (or managed provider). We'll show cost breakdowns in the sheet.
[09:29] Ben: For the PoC what should we expect to instrument for logs and tracing?
[09:34] Rafael: We'll provide tracing hooks and per-route latency logs; Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, model-level latency histograms, and sampling of outputs for quality monitoring.
[09:47] Sofia: Do you have a suggested approach to maintain consistency between re-embeds and incremental updates?
[09:55] Rafael: Maintain embedding version in the index metadata, do shadow re-embed on a subset, measure regressions on your eval set, and then do rolling switch with a small canary. We'll include a playbook.
[10:12] Asha: Any legal/procurement blockers we should surface early?
[10:16] Maya: Standard items: DPA, data residency language, and we can add clauses for encryption controls. If you need specific SLAs beyond standard SLOs we'll flag that early.
[10:30] Ben: Ok. about benchmarks — do you need GPU access from our side?
[10:35] Rafael: No — Redwood can run inference on our Dedicated staging GPUs or we can deploy Private nodes in your VPC that use your infra. For reproducibility, Redwood running the benchmark on our staging provides consistency, but for final acceptance tests you may want it in your environment.
[10:55] Asha: Let's recap quickly.
[11:00] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send PoC plan & pricing; include connector patterns for Milvus/Pinecone, benchmark scripts, and compliance docs. StratusDocs to share anonymized Confluence export + 50-query eval set and confirm target QPS & latency. Schedule benchmark week of 5/18.
[11:20] Ben: Sounds good.
[11:25] Sofia: Thanks, excited to see numbers.
[11:28] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with the doc and calendar invite.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts referenced: PoC Plan (will be sent), Benchmark harness (link placeholder: https://redwood.internal/poc-harness), SOC2 + KMS docs (shared link), Sample pricing sheet (attached in follow up)
